claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: Let v₁,…,v_p be a maximal simple directed path. Every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is the earliest such neighbor, all at least d distinct out-neighbors lie among the p−i vertices v_i,…,v_{p−1}, so p−i≥d. Hence v_i→⋯→v_p→v_i is a directed cycle of length p−i+1≥d+1. Greedy extension and extraction are polynomial. Since every cycle has at most n vertices, n<d+k is a sound NO condition. For k=1 the construction always supplies the required cycle.
claims.witness: A maximal simple directed path v₁,…,v_p and the closing arc v_p→v_i to its earliest out-neighbor witness the constructed cycle.
claims.search_method: Direct proof reconstruction, supplemented by exhaustive Boolean enumeration of every loopless digraph on 2–4 vertices.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For an enumerated distinct directed path P=(v₁,…,v_L), any v_L-to-v₁ path in D−{v₂,…,v_{L−1}} may be chosen simple; its internal vertices are outside P, so its union with P is a simple directed cycle of length at least L. Conversely, any directed cycle of length at least L contains L consecutive vertices forming such a P, while the complementary directed segment is the required return path. There are O(n^L) tuples, and each reachability test costs O(n+m), establishing the stated exact running time.
claims.witness: The certificate is an L-vertex directed path P together with a return path from its last vertex to its first after deleting P's internal vertices.
claims.search_method: Proved both implications and checked the equivalence for every threshold 2≤L≤n+1 on every loopless digraph with 2–4 vertices, totaling 16,584 exact tests.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For any directed cycle C and x∈C∩X, independence makes the predecessor of x lie outside X, and the entering-arc hypothesis therefore places it in S. Different vertices of C∩X have different predecessors because each cycle vertex has a unique successor. Thus |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|, while |C\X|≤n−|X|. Adding gives |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence, disjointness, and the entering-arc condition are all polynomially checkable.
claims.witness: For each cycle C, the injective map x↦pred_C(x) sends C∩X into C∩S.
claims.search_method: Direct predecessor-injection proof, supplemented by exhaustive checking of every eligible disjoint pair X,S in every loopless digraph on 2–4 vertices; 131,755 valid certificates were tested.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: In the stated construction, vertices of Q\{x,y} have outdegree q−1, vertices of A have outdegree q, and x,y have outdegree q−1+a, so d=q−1. After deleting any one vertex, a nonempty complete bidirected Q-core remains, every surviving A-vertex reaches it, and at least one of x,y remains and is reachable from the core and reaches every A-vertex; hence the remainder is strong. Every cycle vertex in A has predecessor x or y, so a cycle contains at most two A-vertices and has length at most q+2. The displayed cycle through all q vertices of Q and two vertices of A has length q+2=d+3. Choosing a≥k−1 yields n=q+a≥q+k−1=d+k, while k≥4 gives d+3<d+k. Letting q grow makes d arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: For q≥3 and a≥max(2,k−1), use the stated Q,A construction. If Q\{x,y}=(z₁,…,z_{q−2}) and a₁,a₂∈A, then x→a₁→z₁→⋯→z_{q−2}→y→a₂→x is a cycle of length q+2, matching the upper bound.
claims.search_method: Parametric degree, connectivity, and circumference proof; additionally checked all 20 instances with 3≤q≤6 and 2≤a≤6 using exact reachability, the upper certificate, and the explicit cycle.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: Start with a directed cycle C in the strong semicomplete input. If c_i→z→c_{i+1}, insert z. Otherwise, for each outside z, cyclic propagation using semicompleteness shows that z either strictly dominates every vertex of C or is strictly dominated by every vertex of C. Strongness forces both classes to be nonempty and, on a path from a C-dominated vertex back to C, supplies an arc u→v from the dominated class to the dominating class. Then c_i→u→v→c_{i+1} enlarges C by two vertices. Repetition yields a Hamiltonian cycle in polynomial time. Since a 2-strong input is strong, n≥d+k is sufficient; it is necessary because no cycle exceeds n vertices.
claims.witness: A sequence of one-vertex insertions and two-vertex bridge insertions enlarges an initial directed cycle to a Hamiltonian directed cycle.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the semicomplete-cycle augmentation proof and exhaustively ran that construction on every strong semicomplete digraph with 2–5 vertices: 52,528 strong instances among 59,808 total, including 19,777 2-strong instances.

target_evidence: The exact target requires an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm for arbitrary 2-strong digraphs. The draft does not provide one: its general exact algorithm has exponent L=d+k, the certificate and obstruction family are structural rather than an FPT decision procedure, and the Hamiltonicity algorithm applies only to semicomplete inputs. The k=1 algorithm, exact linkage formulation, sound upper certificate, explicit 2-strong obstruction family, and polynomial semicomplete special case are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The final writeup explicitly says the general FPT target remains unresolved, so claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is accurate and not overclaimed.
